question: There was a space shuttle flight that launched two days before the original U.S. release date of an episode of The Office that was directed by Jason Reitman. Which member of the crew of this flight was born on the same day as someone who was the head coach of a professional NBA basketball team before 2022? The basketball team was founded after 1988 and was based in the same state the space shuttle flight launched from.

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series)_season_4 "The Office (American TV series) season 4") of the American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy")[television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program")_[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"). It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)

After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot

When [Michael Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scott_(The_Office) "Michael Scott (The Office)") learns that the [Scranton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scranton,_Pennsylvania "Scranton, Pennsylvania") branch's participation in a [Dunder Mifflin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunder_Mifflin "Dunder Mifflin") television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.

Michael asks [Pam Beesly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Beesly "Pam Beesly") to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)[Phyllis Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Vance "Phyllis Vance")'s mission to enlist visiting author [Sue Grafton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_Grafton "Sue Grafton") to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin"), a group of employees write and perform a [jingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle "Jingle") for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. [Andy Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Bernard "Andy Bernard"), meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the [product name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_name "Product name") from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."

[Dwight Schrute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Schrute "Dwight Schrute"), playing in the online virtual world of _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_, has created an [avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(computing) "Avatar (computing)") named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. [Jim Halpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Halpert "Jim Halpert") creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.

Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with [Angela Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Martin "Angela Martin"), Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a [makeout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _[Chariots of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chariots\_of\_Fire\_(instrumental) "Chariots of Fire (instrumental)")_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.

Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes [Fancy Feast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Feast "Fancy Feast") cat food.

## Production

"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and the first episode of the series directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"), who directed the films _[Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno\_(film) "Juno (film)")_ and _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking "Thank You for Smoking")_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on [Creed's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed_Bratton "Creed Bratton") desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother [Jesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Novak "Jesse Novak"), a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by [Craig Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(actor) "Craig Robinson (actor)"), the actor who plays reoccurring character [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin") and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

The _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ was the only non-[reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)

The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a [second unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit "Second unit") shooting Ryan's part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception

"Local Ad" received a 5.2 [Nielsen rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_rating "Nielsen rating") and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)

"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of [Rainn Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainn_Wilson "Rainn Wilson") as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of [Ed Helms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Helms "Ed Helms") as Andy, as well as [Steve Carell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Carell "Steve Carell") as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for [BuddyTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuddyTV "BuddyTV"), praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

For his work on this episode, [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak") was nominated for a [Writers Guild of America Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award "Writers Guild of America Award") for [Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Best_Screenplay_%E2%80%93_Episodic_Comedy "Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy"), but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "[The Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Job_(The_Office) "The Job (The Office)")."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series)_season_4 "The Office (American TV series) season 4") of the American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy")[television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program")_[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"). It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)

After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot

When [Michael Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scott_(The_Office) "Michael Scott (The Office)") learns that the [Scranton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scranton,_Pennsylvania "Scranton, Pennsylvania") branch's participation in a [Dunder Mifflin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunder_Mifflin "Dunder Mifflin") television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.

Michael asks [Pam Beesly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Beesly "Pam Beesly") to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)[Phyllis Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Vance "Phyllis Vance")'s mission to enlist visiting author [Sue Grafton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_Grafton "Sue Grafton") to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin"), a group of employees write and perform a [jingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle "Jingle") for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. [Andy Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Bernard "Andy Bernard"), meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the [product name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_name "Product name") from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."

[Dwight Schrute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Schrute "Dwight Schrute"), playing in the online virtual world of _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_, has created an [avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(computing) "Avatar (computing)") named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. [Jim Halpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Halpert "Jim Halpert") creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.

Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with [Angela Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Martin "Angela Martin"), Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a [makeout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _[Chariots of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chariots\_of\_Fire\_(instrumental) "Chariots of Fire (instrumental)")_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.

Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes [Fancy Feast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Feast "Fancy Feast") cat food.

## Production

"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and the first episode of the series directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"), who directed the films _[Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno\_(film) "Juno (film)")_ and _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking "Thank You for Smoking")_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on [Creed's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed_Bratton "Creed Bratton") desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother [Jesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Novak "Jesse Novak"), a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by [Craig Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(actor) "Craig Robinson (actor)"), the actor who plays reoccurring character [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin") and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

The _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ was the only non-[reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)

The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a [second unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit "Second unit") shooting Ryan's part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception

"Local Ad" received a 5.2 [Nielsen rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_rating "Nielsen rating") and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)

"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of [Rainn Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainn_Wilson "Rainn Wilson") as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of [Ed Helms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Helms "Ed Helms") as Andy, as well as [Steve Carell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Carell "Steve Carell") as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for [BuddyTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuddyTV "BuddyTV"), praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

For his work on this episode, [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak") was nominated for a [Writers Guild of America Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award "Writers Guild of America Award") for [Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Best_Screenplay_%E2%80%93_Episodic_Comedy "Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy"), but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "[The Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Job_(The_Office) "The Job (The Office)")."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

**STS-126** was the one hundred and twenty-fourth [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") mission, and twenty-second orbital flight of the _[Space Shuttle Endeavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Endeavour "Space Shuttle Endeavour")_ (OV-105) to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS).[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5) The purpose of the mission, referred to as **ULF2** by the ISS program, was to deliver equipment and supplies to the station, to service the [Solar Alpha Rotary Joints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Truss_Structure "Integrated Truss Structure") (SARJ), and repair the problem in the starboard SARJ that had limited its use since [STS-120](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120 "STS-120").[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5)[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-overview-6) STS-126 launched on 15 November 2008 at 00:55:39 UTC from [Launch Pad 39A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Launch_Complex_39A "Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A") (LC-39A) at NASA's [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") (KSC) with no delays or issues.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-launch2-7)[[NASA 5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-lb-8)_Endeavour_ successfully docked with the station on 16 November 2008.[[NASA 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-stat05-9) After spending 15 days, 20 hours, 30 minutes, and 30 seconds docked to the station, during which the crew performed four [spacewalks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_activity "Extravehicular activity"), and transferred cargo, the orbiter undocked on 28 November 2008.[[NASA 7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-SR29-10) Due to poor weather at Kennedy Space Center, _Endeavour_ landed at [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base") on 30 November 2008 at 21:25:09 UTC.[[NASA 8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-landingblog-11)

### Crew notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-126&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Crew notes")]

[Joan E. Higginbotham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Higginbotham "Joan Higginbotham") was originally scheduled to fly on STS-126, she was previously mission specialist 4 on [STS-116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-116 "STS-116").[[NASA 9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-crew1-12) On 21 November 2007, NASA announced a change in the crew manifest due to Higginbotham's decision to leave NASA to take a job in the private sector.[[NASA 10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-amend-14) Stephen G. Bowen was originally assigned to [STS-124](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-124 "STS-124") but was moved to STS-126 to allow _Discovery_ to rotate Greg Chamitoff with [Garrett E. Reisman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrett_Reisman "Garrett Reisman").[[NASA 9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-crew1-12)[[NASA 11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-bowen-15)

## Mission payloads

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-126&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mission payloads")]

STS-126 was scheduled to be a sixteen-day mission with four [spacewalks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_activity "Extravehicular activity") (EVA), largely dedicated to servicing and repair of the Solar Alpha Rotary Joints (SARJ).[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5)[[NASA 12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-overview3-16) An additional docked day was added to the flight plan to give the crew more time to complete their tasks.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-EVA4-17) The starboard SARJ had shown anomalous behavior since August 2007, and its use has been minimized pending diagnosis and repair.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-latimes-18)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-sarj1-19) Both the [port and starboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_and_starboard "Port and starboard") SARJs were serviced.[[NASA 13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-overview2-20)[[NASA 14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-summary2-21) In addition to lubricating both [bearings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bearing_(mechanical) "Bearing (mechanical)"), the remaining 11 trundle bearings in the starboard SARJ were replaced.[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-overview-6)[[NASA 13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-overview2-20) Trundle bearing assembly No. 5, one of the 12 assemblies, was removed during an [Expedition 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_16 "Expedition 16") EVA for further examination in December 2007.[[NASA 15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-bearing-22)

STS-126 included the _Leonardo_[Multi-Purpose Logistics Module](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-Purpose_Logistics_Module "Multi-Purpose Logistics Module") (MPLM) on its fifth spaceflight.[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5)_Leonardo_ held over 6,400 kg (14,100 lb) of supplies and equipment. Among the items packed into the MPLM were two new crew quarters racks, a second galley (kitchen) for the _[Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny\_(ISS\_module) "Destiny (ISS module)")_ laboratory, a second Waste and Hygiene Compartment (WHC) rack (lavatory), the [advanced Resistive Exercise Device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Resistive_Exercise_Device "Advanced Resistive Exercise Device") (aRED), two water reclamation racks, spare hardware, and new experiments.[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5)[[NASA 16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-water-23)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-aRED-24) Also included in _Leonardo_ was the [General Laboratory Active Cryogenic ISS Experiment Refrigerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minus_Eighty_Degree_Laboratory_Freezer_for_ISS "Minus Eighty Degree Laboratory Freezer for ISS"), or GLACIER, a double locker cryogenic freezer for transporting and preserving science experiments.[[NASA 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-presskit-5) The shuttle also carried irradiated turkey, [candied yams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candied_yams "Candied yams"), stuffing and dessert for a special [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving_(United_States) "Thanksgiving (United States)") meal at the station, as well as an Official Flight Kit with mementos for those who supported the astronauts and helped them complete their mission successfully.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-lm-25)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-ofk-26) Also carried was a Lightweight MPESS Carrier (LMC) carrying a Flex Hose Rotary Coupler (FHRC) and returning a Nitrogen Assembly Tank from _Quest_ for refurbishment.

### Educational outreach

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-126&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Educational outreach")]

STS-126 carried the signatures of over 500,000 students that participated in the 2008 Student Signatures in Space program, jointly sponsored by NASA and [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-spaceday.org-27) In celebration of Space Day last May 2008, students from over 500 schools signed giant posters, their signatures were scanned onto a disk, and the disk was flown on the STS-126 mission.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-spaceday.org-27) The Student Signatures in Space project has been active since 1997, and has flown student signatures on seven other shuttle flights, starting with [STS-86](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-86 "STS-86").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-spaceday.org-27)

### Agricultural camera (AgCam)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-126&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Agricultural camera (AgCam)")]

Also aboard STS-126 was the [Agricultural Camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AgCam "AgCam") (AgCam) which was installed in the _Destiny_ module and is used to assist farmers and provide educational opportunities for students around the country.[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam-28)[[NASA 18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam2-29) Students and faculty at the [University of North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Dakota "University of North Dakota") built the Agricultural Camera (AgCam), that was to be delivered and installed on the International Space Station.[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam-28) The students will operate the camera from their campus and work with NASA engineers and station astronauts to take visible and [infrared light images](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared "Infrared") of growing crops, grasslands, forests and wetlands in the [Great Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") and [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") regions.[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam-28)[[NASA 18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam2-29)

The information from AgCam provided data to agricultural producers in [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota") and neighboring states, benefiting farmers and ranchers and providing ways for them to protect the environment. AgCam imagery also may assist in disaster management, such as flood monitoring and wild fire mapping.[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-AgCam-28)

### Cow embryos and pig cells in space

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-126&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cow embryos and pig cells in space")]

STS-126 also flew the first bovine [embryos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo "Embryo") as well as porcine embryonic stem cells on an American spacecraft for an experiment to evaluate effects of the environment of space on embryonic development. The project was a joint project of ZeroGravity Inc., [University of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florida "University of Florida") and [USDA ARS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_Research_Service "Agricultural Research Service").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-126#cite_note-embryos-30)
