### _Harmony_ (Node 2)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Harmony (Node 2)")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/ISS_Node_2_module.jpg/250px-ISS_Node_2_module.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS_Node_2_module.jpg)

_Harmony_ under assembly at the SSPF

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/STS120Lightsaber.jpg/250px-STS120Lightsaber.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120Lightsaber.jpg)

Astronaut [Jim Reilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_F._Reilly "James F. Reilly") helped welcome [R2-D2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R2-D2 "R2-D2") and [Luke Skywalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Skywalker "Luke Skywalker")'s [lightsaber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightsaber "Lightsaber") from _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ to the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center").

STS-120 delivered launch package 10A to the International Space Station (ISS).[[NASA 5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-harm1-14) It consisted of the U.S. _[Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony\_(ISS\_module) "Harmony (ISS module)")_ module (also known as Node 2), with four DC-to-DC Converter Unit (DDCU) racks and three Zero-g Storage Racks (ZSR) installed; a Power and Data Grapple Fixture (PDGF) for the station's robot arm, and a Shuttle Power Distribution Unit (SPDU). _Harmony_ was manufactured for NASA by [Thales Alenia Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Alenia_Space "Thales Alenia Space") in [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"), Italy, as part of an agreement between NASA and the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") and was the first pressurized habitable module delivered to the station since the [_Pirs_ docking compartment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirs_(ISS_module) "Pirs (ISS module)") was installed in August 2001.

Since STS-120 docked to the [Pressurized Mating Adapter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressurized_Mating_Adapter "Pressurized Mating Adapter")-2 (PMA-2) on the forward port of the _[Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny\_(ISS\_module) "Destiny (ISS module)")_ module, installation of _Harmony_ occurred in two stages: STS-120 installed _Harmony_ to the port node of the _Unity_ module. After _Discovery_ undocked, the [station's robotic arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm2 "Canadarm2") detached PMA-2 from _Destiny_, and moved it to the forward port of _Harmony_. Following the relocation of PMA-2, the robotic arm was used to move _Harmony_ from its initial position to its final position, on the forward port of _Destiny_.[[NASA 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-pma3-15)

The final positioning of _Harmony_ allowed for the later installation of the [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESA "ESA")_[Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus\_(ISS\_module) "Columbus (ISS module)")_ and [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA")_[Kibō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_Experiment\_Module "Japanese Experiment Module")_ research modules, which were attached to the side ports of _Harmony_.

### P6 relocation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: P6 relocation")]

During STS-120, the [P6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S6_truss "S6 truss") solar arrays were moved from the [Z1 truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z1_truss "Z1 truss") on top of _Unity_, to their final position at the port end of the truss.

### Outreach

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Outreach")]

STS-120 carried the signatures of over 500,000 students that participated in the 2007 Student Signatures in Space program, jointly sponsored by NASA and Lockheed Martin.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nwi-16)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-hobart-17) In celebration of Space Day in May 2007, students from over 500 schools around the world signed giant posters. Their signatures were scanned onto a disk, and the disk was manifested on the STS-120 mission.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nwi-16)

Also during STS-120, the [lightsaber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightsaber "Lightsaber") used by actor [Mark Hamill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hamill "Mark Hamill") in the 1983 film _[Return of the Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_the\_Jedi "Return of the Jedi")_ was flown to the station and returned to Earth.[[NASA 7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-Whatsgoingup-18) Stowed on-board _Discovery_ for the length of the mission, the [prop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_property "Theatrical property") was flown in honor of the 30th anniversary of the _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ franchise.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19) On August 28, 2007, [Chewbacca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chewbacca "Chewbacca") from the _Star Wars_ films presented the lightsaber to NASA officials from [Space Center Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Center_Houston "Space Center Houston"), in an official ceremony at [Oakland International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_International_Airport "Oakland International Airport").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19) The lightsaber was then flown to Houston, where it was greeted by [Stormtroopers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_stormtrooper "Imperial stormtrooper"). The lightsaber will be displayed at Space Center Houston.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19)

## Mission background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mission background")]

At the time of the _[Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Columbia\_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster")_ disaster, STS-120 was scheduled for early 2004. It was delayed repeatedly until October 23, 2007.

NASA originally scheduled the launch for October 20, 2007, but due to the International Space Station program requirement, launch was delayed to October 23, 2007.[[NASA 8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tv-20)

In light of the small gouge to the underside of _Endeavour_ that occurred on [STS-118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-118 "STS-118"), in August 2007, NASA managers announced that they expected to add a fifth spacewalk to the STS-120 mission, designed to test a heat-shield repair tool.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-goo-21) The repair technique was originally scheduled for a flight in 2008, but following STS-118, it was decided to move up the testing. The repair tool, called a [TPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_thermal_protection_system "Space Shuttle thermal protection system") (thermal protection system) repair [ablator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ablation "Ablation") dispenser (T-RAD), has never been tested in space, so the spacewalk would have allowed managers to evaluate its effectiveness in low gravity environments.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva5-22) During the course of the mission, issues with the [S4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Truss_Structure#P3/P4,_S3/S4_truss_assemblies "Integrated Truss Structure")[starboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboard "Starboard")[Solar Alpha Rotary Joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Alpha_Rotary_Joint "Solar Alpha Rotary Joint") (SARJ), and P6 Solar Array, deferred this test objective to a future mission.

The mission marked:[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-ql-5)

*   151st NASA crewed spaceflight
*   120th Space Shuttle flight since [STS-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-1 "STS-1")
*   34th flight of _[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_
*   95th post-_[Challenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Challenger\_disaster "Space Shuttle Challenger disaster")_ mission
*   7th post-_Columbia_ mission

## Mission timeline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mission timeline")]

### Launch preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Launch preparations")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/STS120_at_Pad.jpg/250px-STS120_at_Pad.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120_at_Pad.jpg)

_[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_ moved to [LC-39A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LC-39A "LC-39A") on September 30, 2007.

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/VABmating_STS-120.jpg/250px-VABmating_STS-120.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VABmating_STS-120.jpg)

_Discovery's_[external tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_external_tank "Space Shuttle external tank") mated to the [Solid Rocket Boosters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_rocket_booster "Solid rocket booster").

Following STS-118 in August 2007, NASA managers decided to make modifications to the [external tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_external_tank "Space Shuttle external tank") to be used on STS-120, and modify the [liquid oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_oxygen "Liquid oxygen") feed-line brackets.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cbs-23) The change involved a new low-density foam application, and thinner gaskets. Shuttle Program Managers decided to do this to reduce the foam loss from the area that had been noted since [STS-114](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-114 "STS-114")'s "Return to Flight" mission in 2005. STS-118 had a small gouge on the belly of the orbiter due to a chunk of foam that impacted during launch in August 2007. The week of September 17, 2007, NASA managers decided to delay _Discovery's_ rollover to the [Vehicle Assembly Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_Assembly_Building "Vehicle Assembly Building") (VAB), due to a hydraulic fluid leak from the right main landing gear strut. The strut repair was successfully completed on September 19, 2007. _Discovery_ then moved to the VAB, and was mated to the External Tank and [Solid Rocket Boosters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_rocket_booster "Solid rocket booster"). Perched atop the [mobile launcher platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_launcher_platform "Mobile launcher platform"), _Discovery_ arrived at Launch complex 39A on September 30, 2007.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-pad-24)[[NASA 9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-autogenerated1-25)

The crew of STS-120 arrived at Kennedy Space Center on October 7, 2007, and began final preparations, including the [terminal countdown demonstration test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_countdown_demonstration_test "Terminal countdown demonstration test"), or "Dress Rehearsal", scheduled for October 7, 2007, through October 10, 2007.[[NASA 10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tcdt2-26)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-esatcdt-27)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tcdt-28)

On October 9, 2007, NASA's Engineering and Safety Center, an independent review group set up after the 2003 _Columbia_ disaster, advised replacement of three of _Discovery's_[reinforced carbon-carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforced_carbon-carbon "Reinforced carbon-carbon") (RCC) panels on the leading wing edge, due to a loss of small amounts of the protective [silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon "Silicon")-[carbide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbide "Carbide") coating.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-delay-29)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cbca-30) NASA reviewed the issue of oxidation of the panels for several months, using a variety of specialized testing methods, including [thermography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermography "Thermography").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-update1-31)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-abcdelay-32) These tests showed that the panels had not worsened over the course of the past two flights of _Discovery_, and the orbiter project engineers concluded in August that _Discovery_ was safe to launch as is.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cbca-30)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-update1-31)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-itwire-33) Had a decision been made to repair the panels, the orbiter would have been rolled back to the VAB, delaying the launch.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-delay-29)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cbca-30)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-update1-31)

On October 16, 2007, NASA Managers completed the Flight Readiness Review, and held a press conference to announce the mission plan.[[NASA 11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-conf-34) The issue of the RCC panels raised by NESC was found to be of little immediate concern, because the NESC took pre-flight thermography data from _Endeavour_ and compared it with _Discovery_, but there was no commonality in flight history between the two vehicles.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-FRR-35) The research showed no significant difference between the panels prior to STS-114, and the panels today, which indicates the coating has not worsened during the previous flights, adding confidence that _Discovery's_ RCC panels have had no deterioration in the flights since.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-FRR-35) NASA announced on the main shuttle page that "The Space Shuttle Program has determined that Discovery's astronauts can safely carry out their mission without having to replace the panels."[[NASA 12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-go-36)

### October 23 (Flight Day 1, Launch)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: October 23 (Flight Day 1, Launch)")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/STS120LaunchHiRes-edit1.jpg/250px-STS120LaunchHiRes-edit1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120LaunchHiRes-edit1.jpg)

STS-120 begins its mission.

_Discovery_ launched on time at 11:38 [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time") (15:38 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC "UTC")).[[NASA 13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-STS-120-01-37)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-lat-38) In the countdown's final minutes, a piece of ice, measuring 4 inches (10 cm) x .5 inches (1.3 cm) was seen on the hydrogen umbilical between the orbiter and the external tank.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fox-20071024-39) The inspection team was called back to the pad (a contingency that has been practiced, and used before), to get a closer look at the ice build-up. NASA flight controllers deemed it too small to pose a threat to the thermal protection system. The ice was attached to a [Kapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapton "Kapton") purge barrier near the LH2 umbilical [pyrotechnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrotechnic_fastener "Pyrotechnic fastener") canister closeout.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nsf1-40) It had been shown in tests that ice on this liner, sometimes called a "baggie", would likely come off at main engine ignition.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-41) Had it been on other metal surfaces around the liner, this may have posed a threat of staying on and breaking off at a critical part of launch. Despite these issues, the launch continued as planned. The forecast for launch initially was a 60% chance of weather prohibiting launch, and although the launch team weather officers were tracking an incoming storm, the weather remained favorable for launch.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-weather-42) Present for the launch was [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas"), to see off the Star Wars lightsaber.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-wired-43) In a press briefing following launch, NASA managers noted a few "events" involving debris, but they occurred later in ascent, after the period of maximum aerodynamic [velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity "Velocity") and speed, and were not concerning.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nyt-44)

### October 24 (Flight day 2)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: October 24 (Flight day 2)")]

The crew of STS-120 spent their first full day in space by performing the RCC survey, using the [Shuttle Remote Manipulator System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm "Canadarm") (SRMS), and the [Orbiter Boom Sensor System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbiter_Boom_Sensor_System "Orbiter Boom Sensor System") (OBSS).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-harwood1-45) The crew also worked on various tasks such as inspecting the [Extravehicular Mobility Units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_Mobility_Unit "Extravehicular Mobility Unit") (EMUs, or spacesuits) that will be used on the EVAs, and doing some preliminary work to get ready for docking with the International Space Station on Thursday.[[NASA 14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr3-46) Deputy Shuttle Program Manager and Mission Management Team (MMT) chairman John Shannon noted during the status briefing that the preliminary data the team had reviewed showed no items of concern, and the ascent imagery showed no significant losses prior to SRB separation.[[NASA 15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-SR4-47)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-CBS2-48) Shannon said there were several items the team was waiting for higher resolution imagery to assess, including a possible protruding gap filler, and some external tank foam losses, but there was nothing to indicate any problems.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nsf1-40) Shannon also noted that a vapor trail was seen coming off the external tank for several seconds during launch, but noted that this was a condition seen during both STS-114, and [STS-121](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-121 "STS-121"), and was found to be condensate coming off the back side of the tank. Due to the temperature and humidity, combined with the angle of the Sun for _Discovery's_ launch, the plume appeared more dramatic in some of the imagery. This was considered an "expected condition", and Shannon confirmed it was of no concern.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nsf1-40)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-CBS2-48)

### October 25 (Flight day 3)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: October 25 (Flight day 3)")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Space_Shuttle_Discovery.png/250px-Space_Shuttle_Discovery.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Space_Shuttle_Discovery.png)

Backdropped by a blue and white Earth, Space Shuttle _Discovery_ approaches the International Space Station.

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Whitson_greets_Melroy.jpg/250px-Whitson_greets_Melroy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Whitson_greets_Melroy.jpg)

Whitson (right), Expedition 16 commander, greets STS-120 commander Melroy after opening the hatches between the station and the shuttle.

The crew of STS-120 worked through the rendezvous procedures in the morning leading to the [rendezvous pitch maneuver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendezvous_pitch_maneuver "Rendezvous pitch maneuver") which began at 11:34 UTC. Following the RPM, the crew was given the "Go" to dock with the station, and successful docking to the International Space Station occurred at 12:40 UTC.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-docking-49)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-upi-50) Following docking, the joint crews conducted a station safety review, and Tani's custom Soyuz seatliner was transferred from _Discovery_ to the [Soyuz TMA-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-11 "Soyuz TMA-11"), with Anderson's seat liner taken into _Discovery_. This marked the official end of Expedition 16 for Anderson, and the start of Tani's increment.[[NASA 16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr6-51) Just before the two crews signed off to sleep, they were informed that after preliminary review of the RPM photography, focused inspection of the orbiter's heat shield would not be required.[[NASA 16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr6-51)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day3update-52) During the MMT briefing, Shannon confirmed that initial evaluation of the available data showed _Discovery_ to be a "pretty clean vehicle". He also confirmed they were not working any issues or items of interest. Shannon said the piece of ice that was looked at prior to launch dislodged during main engine ignition, and as it fell, the ice appeared to graze the underside of the orbiter at the beginning of ascent, but the area around the impact site was in good condition, and the ice did not appear to have caused any damage.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day3update-52) Shannon said the teams would continue to evaluate the imagery and data, but the shuttle was in a good configuration.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-franks-53)

### October 26 (Flight day 4)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: October 26 (Flight day 4)")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/STS120_EVA1Wheelock.jpg/250px-STS120_EVA1Wheelock.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120_EVA1Wheelock.jpg)

Wheelock prepares for his first EVA. Behind him, Parazynski floats upside down.

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/STS120HarmonyInstalled.jpg/250px-STS120HarmonyInstalled.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120HarmonyInstalled.jpg)

The interior of _Harmony_ as seen following its attachment to the ISS on flight day 5.

The two crews started the day by preparing for the mission's first spacewalk, which began at 10:02 UTC, and ended at 16:16 UTC. Parazynski and Wheelock successfully completed all EVA activities, including preparing _Harmony_ for removal from the payload bay.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-harmmate-54) Wilson, Tani, and Anderson controlled the station's robotic arm, moving _Harmony_ out of the bay and onto the port side of the [_Unity_ node](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unity_Module "Unity Module"). At 15:38 UTC, _Harmony_ was officially mated to the space station.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-harmmate-54)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-room-55) The station's new addition adds 2,666 cubic feet (75.5 m 3) to the station's living volume, an increase of almost 20%, from 15,000 cubic feet (420 m 3) to 17,666 cubic feet (500.2 m 3).[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr8-56)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-addition-57)

At the Mission Management Team meeting, managers cleared _Discovery's_ heat shield for reentry, and verified that focused inspection was not required, but noted that late inspection will still be performed on flight day 13 following undocking.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-room-55)[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr8-56)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fi-58) John Shannon mentioned that managers have decided to add a task to the second EVA, asking the astronauts to visually inspect the Solar Alpha Rotary Joint (SARJ) on the starboard side, as the joint has registered some vibration for the past month and a half. While the friction is not constant or severe, managers will have Tani remove the insulation covers from the joint to photograph the swing bolts on the joint since Tani would be near the area during the EVA.[[NASA 17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr8-56)

### October 27 (Flight day 5)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: October 27 (Flight day 5)")]

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/STS120_Day_7_Harmony_Model.jpg/250px-STS120_Day_7_Harmony_Model.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120_Day_7_Harmony_Model.jpg)

Stephanie Wilson floats with a model of _Harmony_ on the middeck of _Discovery_.

The two crews worked to prepare _Harmony_ for entry in the morning, connecting power and data cables, and at 12:24 UTC, the hatch was opened, and the crew was allowed to enter.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-entered-59) Whitson, Malenchenko, and Nespoli entered first, wearing masks, and installed a temporary air duct to the node, to allow the air inside to circulate through the station's filters.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-entered-59) Until the air is fully exchanged, occupancy of the node is limited to only a few crew members at a time, and they are not to remain inside for extended periods. Some of the work the crew has to do inside the node is to remove approximately 700 screws and bolts that are holding down equipment and panels, placed for security during launch, but not needed in space.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-entered-59) After allowing the ventilation system work for several hours, the two crews participated in a press conference with [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS"), [Fox News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News "Fox News"), and [WHAM-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHAM-TV "WHAM-TV") from inside _Harmony_.[[NASA 18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr10-60)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day5-61)

### October 28 (Flight day 6)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: October 28 (Flight day 6)")]

The two crews awoke at 05:08 UTC, and began preparing for the second EVA. Parazynski and Tani began the spacewalk at 09:32 UTC, a half-hour ahead of the planned timeline.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva2-62) The pair started with the P6 truss, removing the attachments to the Z1 truss, which allowed Wilson and Wheelock to use the station's robotic arm to move the truss to a position where it was "parked" for the night.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva2-62)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cnnday6-63) Joking to Wilson "Don't drop it!", Parazynski then moved on and installed handrails onto _Harmony_, while Tani went to inspect some items requested by the managers, including handrails on a Crew and Equipment Translation Aid (CETA) cart, that was considered as a possible cause of [Rick Mastracchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Mastracchio "Richard Mastracchio")'s glove tear on STS-118.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cnnday6-63) Tani noted the handrail appeared to be intact, with no obvious sharp edges.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva2-62) Tani then moved on to the Solar Alpha Rotary Joint (SARJ) that has had an intermittent vibration for over a month. After removing the cover from the joint, Tani called down to the team to let them know he saw some metal shavings, and some wear patterns and discoloration on one of the rings inside the joint.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day6-64) "It's like the result that you get with the metal, iron filings and you put a magnet under it and they stand straight up."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva2-62) Tani collected some of the shavings onto some tape, which returned to Earth with the shuttle for further analysis.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva2-62) Managers decided to add a task to Tuesday's EVA, having Parazynski inspect the port (left side) SARJ, using photography and video to compare it to the starboard SARJ inspected by Tani.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day7CBS-65)

### October 29 (Flight day 7)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: October 29 (Flight day 7)")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/STS-120_Two_Crews.jpg/250px-STS-120_Two_Crews.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS-120_Two_Crews.jpg)

The two crews took time out to participate in a joint crew news conference, and to pose for a crew photo.

The two crews used the morning to move the P6 truss from its overnight position on the station's robotic arm, over to the shuttle's robotic arm. The crew then moved the station's arm along the [mobile transporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm2#Mobile_Base_System "Canadarm2") to an outboard work site that allows attachment of the P6 truss to its new location on the [P5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P5_spacer_truss_segment "P5 spacer truss segment") truss on Tuesday.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day7CBS-65)[[NASA 19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-SR13-66) Managers on the ground had Whitson perform an experiment on the shavings Tani collected from the SARJ on Sunday's EVA, putting a magnet under a slip of paper, and testing to see if the shavings collected on the paper, to ascertain if they were metal.[[NASA 20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-briefing-67) The test confirmed the particles collected by Tani were [ferrous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrous "Ferrous"). This information allowed the managers on the ground to rule out some possibilities of the origin of the particles, such as the thermal covers, which are made of aluminized mylar.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-reutday7-68)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-FD7SR-69)

The Mission Management Team discussed the SARJ issues with the ISS team, and decided to add an extra docked day to the mission, between flight days 11 and 12.[[NASA 21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-SR14-70) The new plan changed the objectives of EVA four from the heat shield repair materials testing, to a more thorough inspection of the starboard SARJ.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-spacefacts-sts120-13) With the new flight plan, _Discovery_ would undock on November 5, 2007, with a landing on November 7, 2007, at approximately 05:11 EST.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-FD7SR-69)

### October 30 (Flight day 8)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: October 30 (Flight day 8)")]

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/STS120SolarPanel.jpg/250px-STS120SolarPanel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120SolarPanel.jpg)

Image taken from a camera mounted on the space station, shows an apparent tear in the 4B solar array, with a smaller separation to the right.

The two crews spent the morning preparing for the mission's third EVA, which began at 08:45 UTC.[[NASA 22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day8sr16-71) The EVA completed the installation of the P6 solar arrays onto the P5 truss, and the rest of the EVA activities were accomplished successfully, with the EVA ending at 15:53 UTC. Once the P6 solar array was attached, the process of deploying the arrays began. The first set of arrays, 2B, was successfully deployed with no issues, but during the deployment of the 4B array, the crew halted when they noticed an abnormality.[[NASA 22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day8sr16-71) Initial images taken by the crew and station cameras showed what appeared to be a tear in a small portion of the array.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-array-72)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-bbctear-73) During a press briefing, ISS Program Manager Mike Suffredini said the crew took high resolution images of the solar array, and the managers would analyze the images overnight to determine a course of action.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-franksday8-74) Sufredini mentioned that with the array in the 90% unfurled position, it was still generating 97% of the expected power to the station, only slightly less than a fully unfurled array.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day8rip-75)

### October 31 (Flight day 9)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: October 31 (Flight day 9)")]

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/STS120President_Bush.jpg/250px-STS120President_Bush.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120President_Bush.jpg)

Former President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") and the former [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady "First Lady") talk to the STS-120 astronauts and the Expedition 16 crewmembers during a visit to the [Mission Control Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Control_Center "Mission Control Center"), at [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson_Space_Center "Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center") in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston").

The crew began the day working through a variety of tasks, including preparing for the fourth EVA, installing a Zero Gravity Stowage Rack in _Harmony_, and working with some of the experiments on board.[[NASA 23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr17-76) Nespoli and Melroy participated in a Public Affairs event (PAO), and received a call from the President of Italy, [Giorgio Napolitano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Napolitano "Giorgio Napolitano"). The entire crew took part in a second PAO event, fielding calls from news agencies from the United States, Europe, and Russia.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day9spacecom-77) Around 15:00 UTC, mission control informed the crew that Thursday's planned EVA would be postponed to either Friday, or perhaps Saturday, to allow for a new EVA plan to be worked out, which would include troubleshooting of the P6 solar arrays.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day9spacecom-77)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day9nyt-78)

### November 1 (Flight day 10)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: November 1 (Flight day 10)")]

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/STS120_Cufflink.jpg/250px-STS120_Cufflink.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120_Cufflink.jpg)

STS-120 pilot George Zamka holds a newly manufactured "cufflink" apparatus, one of five cufflinks assembled by crewmembers. The cufflink is designed to take the structural load off of the damaged hinges of the P6 4B solar array.

Shortly after awakening in the morning, the crew was informed that the managers had chosen to take an extra day to evaluate and plan the fourth EVA.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day10spacecom-79) Managers initially planned for the EVA to be done on flight day 11, but would use an extra day to conduct further analysis and allow the crew to have extra time to make the tools and equipment needed, and to review and practice the procedures.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day10spacecom-79)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nsfday10-80) The crew took some time out to gather in the _Harmony_ module to speak with former president [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") and his wife, Barbara, who were visiting Johnson Space Center.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-president-81)

The rest of the day was devoted to assembling and configuring the new equipment and tools that would be required for the solar array repair, including a tool termed a "cufflink". The tear in the array is located at one of the hinges, which carries the load of the array, so the cufflink will be a load-bearing strap to relieve the pressure from the snagged area, transferring the load from the hinge, to the cufflink.[[NASA 24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr19-82)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-priority-83) The cufflink is made up of two wires, with two tabs at the end, that are threaded through existing reinforced aluminum holes in the solar array panels.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cufflink-84) The EVA plans call for the space station's robotic arm to grapple the shuttle's orbital inspection boom, with an extension on the end, to allow Parazynski to reach the solar array while positioned on a foot restraint at the end of the system.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cufflink-84) Wheelock will be watching to let the team know the clearances, and to assist Parazynski and the robotics team with positioning.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cufflink-84) With the changes to the timeline, the crew would be shifting their sleep schedule, to allow for a daylight landing on Wednesday, rather than the early morning landing that was originally planned. The fifth EVA that was planned for the Expedition 16 crew during the mission was delayed, and will be performed by the station crew after the shuttle departs.[[NASA 24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr19-82)

### November 2 (Flight day 11)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: November 2 (Flight day 11)")]

The shuttle and station crews spent the day discussing the new EVA plan with managers on the ground, reviewing the procedures, completing the tool configurations, and going over the timeline for the fourth EVA, scheduled for Saturday.[[NASA 25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day11SR22-85)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva4nsf-86) The crew also positioned the station's mobile transporter and robotic arm on the end of the truss, to allow the apparatus to reach the solar array. Saturday's EVA would be the first operational use of the Orbiter Boom Sensor System (OBSS) to reach a worksite, although the task was tested and demonstrated during STS-121 to show the boom could provide a stable work platform for EVA activities.[[NASA 25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day11SR22-85)

### November 3 (Flight day 12)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: November 3 (Flight day 12)")]

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/STS120EVA4.jpg/250px-STS120EVA4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120EVA4.jpg)

Astronaut Scott Parazynski at the end of the Orbiter Boom Sensor System performing the solar array repair.

After being awakened by the theme music from _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_music "Star Wars music")_, the station and shuttle crews got to work preparing for the mission's fourth EVA.[[NASA 25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day11SR22-85)[[NASA 26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day12SR23-87) The spacewalk began at 10:03 UTC. After translating out to the robotic arm, Parazynski attached himself to the adjustable portable foot restraint (APFR), and was taken to the solar array worksite.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-rightabc-88)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-day12reuters-89) Working slowly, with direction from Wheelock and the ground team, Parazynski secured the five cufflinks to the array, and then backed away to observe the deploy action.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-successarray-90)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nytrepair-91) Inside the station, the crew deployed the array a half a "bay" at a time, and the array was fully deployed at 15:23 UTC.[[NASA 27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-deploy-92) After performing additional inspections of both the 2B, and 4B arrays, Parazynski and Wheelock finished the EVA at 17:22 UTC.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva4nsf-86) With the mission's final spacewalk completed, Parazynski has completed seven EVAs, for a total time of 47 hours, 05 minutes, placing him 5th overall for total EVA duration.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sfnday12-93) Wheelock completed three EVAs, for a total time of 20 hours, 41 minutes, and the total EVA time for STS-120 was 27 hours, 14 minutes.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sfnday12-93)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva4ends-94) During the EVA, a pair of [needlenose pliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needlenose_pliers "Needlenose pliers") floated free of the equipment, and was observed floating nearby the window by the crew inside the station. The tool floated clear of the station, and was not a hazard.[[NASA 28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-exfd13-95)

### November 4 (Flight day 13)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: November 4 (Flight day 13)")]

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/ISS_after_STS-120_in_November_2007.jpg/250px-ISS_after_STS-120_in_November_2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS_after_STS-120_in_November_2007.jpg)

The International Space Station as seen following undocking. The P6 solar array is visible on the right.

The Shuttle and station crews spent the day transferring cargo, and resting in preparation for Monday's departure of _Discovery_. Nespoli and Melroy spent some time in the morning speaking to the Italian media, and later in the day the crew had some off-duty time. Following the traditional farewell ceremony, the hatches were closed at 20:03 UTC.[[NASA 29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-hatches-96) During the emotional ceremony, Anderson spoke to the ground crew, expressing his gratitude for their support during his 137 days as an Expedition crewmember.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-farewellsfn-97)

> You all kept me safe, you've shown me unwavering patience and professionalism... And you've all overlooked my shortcomings, and it's my hope that maybe you've even had a few laughs along the way... What I'd like to say is: What we are doing here is very important for all of human kind. It's worth the risk, it's worth the cost, and you folks on the ground are the people who make it happen. So I want you to take pride in your work and constantly look toward the heavens, for it is there you will see your future. For all the flight control, training and engineering teams in Houston, Huntsville and Moscow... I say thank you, you are indeed the best and the brightest that our world has to offer.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-farewellsfn-97)

—Clayton Anderson

### November 5 (Flight day 14)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: November 5 (Flight day 14)")]

The two crews spent the morning preparing for _Discovery's_ undocking from the International Space Station.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-undockabc-98) At 10:32 UTC, the orbiter successfully backed away from the Pressurized Mating Adapter on the _Destiny_ Laboratory, and pilot Zamka began the fly-around to allow the shuttle crew to photograph the new configuration of the station.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-undocking-99)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-departsfn-100) After performing the final separation burn, focused inspection began, to scan the wing leading edges and nose cap, the final analysis that allows the ground team to clear the orbiter for re-entry on Wednesday.[[NASA 30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr28-101)

### November 6 (Flight day 15)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: November 6 (Flight day 15)")]

The crew of _Discovery_ spent the day preparing Wednesday's landing.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tests-102) In addition to doing final packing and stowing activities, Melroy and Zamka did a check of the orbiter's systems, including the flight control systems, and the reaction control system jets.[[NASA 31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-sr30-103) The crew took some time out in the morning to speak to the media, and then had a deorbit preparation briefing with the ground team. Melroy performed a burn of the orbiter's engines in the afternoon, an orbit adjustment burn done to refine the orbiter's trajectory for the two Wednesday landing opportunities at Kennedy Space Center. NASA managers officially cleared _Discovery'_ s heat shield for landing after reviewing the data sent down by the final inspection on Monday.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-cleared-104)

### November 7 (Flight day 16, Landing)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: November 7 (Flight day 16, Landing)")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/STS120LandingKSC.jpg/250px-STS120LandingKSC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120LandingKSC.jpg)

_Discovery_ makes a smooth landing at the Shuttle Landing Facility, wrapping up a 15-day mission to deliver the _Harmony_ module to the International Space Station.

The crew of _Discovery_ got to work preparing for landing following their wake up call. NASA did not activate either [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base"), or [White Sands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_Missile_Range "White Sands Missile Range"), as the weather looked favorable for both [landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle#Re-entry_and_landing "Space Shuttle") opportunities at Kennedy. The weather forecast at the [Shuttle Landing Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shuttle_Landing_Facility "Shuttle Landing Facility") called for good visibility, with mostly sunny skies, although the headwinds would be evaluated, as they had been peaking at 23 knots (43 km/h). Due to the sleep shifting done by the crew earlier in the mission to schedule the extra mission days, the landing was done on what is called a "descending" node entry. Unlike ascending node entries, this entry trajectory brought the shuttle diagonally across the United States for the first time since [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"). The shuttle passed over Vancouver, [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"), Canada, and angled down towards Florida.[[NASA 32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tracks-105) Once the orbiter reached Florida, Melroy performed a 195-degree right overhead turn along the heading alignment cone (HAC) in order to line up for a landing on Runway 33.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tests-102) The first landing opportunity began with a deorbit burn at 16:59 UTC and finished with a landing at 13:01 EST.[[NASA 32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tracks-105) The deorbit burns were done to slow the orbiter's speed and to drop it out of freefall orbit and on target for the designated runway.[[NASA 33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-landing101-106)

_Discovery's_ payload bay doors were closed at 14:13 UTC, and the crew began fluid loading at 16:00 UTC. Fluid loading is a procedure that involves drinking high salt content fluids, which allows the astronauts to adjust to the return to gravity, and reduces the chance of [hypotension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypotension "Hypotension") upon returning to Earth.[[NASA 34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fl-107)[[NASA 35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-landingupdates-108) Shortly after 16:00 UTC, the crew began to get into their launch and entry suits, and ingress into their respective seats for landing.[[NASA 35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-landingupdates-108) At 16:50 UTC, Entry Flight Director [Bryan Lunney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Lunney "Bryan Lunney") gave the crew the "go" for deorbit burn. The initiation of the burn committed _Discovery_ to landing. The burn was initiated at 16:59 UTC, and was one minute and 53 seconds in duration.[[NASA 35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-landingupdates-108) The deorbit burn is performed while the orbiter is facing opposite its direction of travel, which allows the engines to act as a braking system, slowing its speed by approximately 215 feet per second (66 m/s). After the burn, the remaining propellant in the orbiter's maneuvering thrusters was dumped overboard, at 17:13 UTC.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-liveupdate-109)_Discovery_ began to feel the effects of gravity around 400,000 feet (120,000 m), as it traveled above the North Pacific Ocean at 17:30 UTC.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-liveupdate-109) As the orbiter descended, Melroy initiated a series of "rolls", and roll reversals, which serve to create friction and bleed off additional speed. At 17:40 UTC, _Discovery_ entered the United States, flying over [Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana "Montana"). At 17:53, the orbiter entered Florida, flying at a speed of 3,500 mph (5,600 km/h), and an altitude of 118,000 feet (36,000 m).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-liveupdate-109)

_Discovery_ touched down on runway 33 at 13:01:18 EST, the rear landing gear touching down first, the nose gear touching down at 13:01:32 EDT, and the orbiter came to a complete stop at 13:02:13 EDT.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-liveupdate-109)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nytland-110) Total mission time was 15 days, 2 hours, 23 minutes, 55 seconds, for a distance of 6.25 million miles in 238 orbits.[[NASA 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-finalsr-1)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-klotzlanding-111) The completion of STS-120 marks the longest duration mission for _Discovery_.

## ESA _Esperia_ Mission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: ESA Esperia Mission")]

Italian astronaut **Paolo Nespoli** participated in the European Space Agency's (ESA) _Esperia_ mission as part of his involvement in the STS-120 Space Shuttle flight to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS) in October 2007.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-esa-esperia-112)

The Esperia mission was a scientific program coordinated by ESA and the [Italian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Space_Agency "Italian Space Agency") (ASI), with the objective of conducting a suite of biomedical and biological experiments in microgravity. According to the official STS-120 press kit, Nespoli served as a flight engineer aboard [Expedition 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_16 "Expedition 16") and was responsible for executing five scientific experiments provided by the European science community.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nasa-presskit-113)

Two of the experiments – **Chromosome‐2** and **Neocytolysis** – were sponsored by ESA. These aimed to investigate changes in gene expression and red blood cell destruction under microgravity conditions, respectively. The remaining three – **HPA**, **FRTL‐5**, and **SPORE** – were supported by ASI.

*   **HPA** (Human Pathways Alteration) studied alterations in protein expression due to spaceflight.
*   **FRTL‐5** involved cultured thyroid cells to observe cellular behavior in microgravity.
*   **SPORE** (Spore Test) evaluated the survival and mutation rates of fungal spores in space.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-asi-esperia-114)

The scientific results contributed to the understanding of human adaptation and biological responses to the space environment, with potential applications in both space exploration and terrestrial medicine.

## Contingency mission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Contingency mission")]

**[STS-320](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-3xx "STS-3xx")** was the designation given to the [Contingency Shuttle Crew Support](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contingency_Shuttle_Crew_Support "Contingency Shuttle Crew Support") mission which would have been launched in the event Space Shuttle _Discovery_ became disabled during STS-120.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-manifest2-116) It would have been a modified version of the [STS-122](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-122 "STS-122") mission, which would have involved the launch date being brought forward. If it had been needed, it would have been launched no later than January 5, 2008. The crew for this mission would have been a four-person subset of the full STS-122 crew.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-manifest2-116)

**STS-120** was a [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS) that launched on October 23, 2007, from the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center"), Florida.[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-main-6) The mission is also referred to as **ISS-10A** by the ISS program. STS-120 delivered the _[Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony\_(ISS\_module) "Harmony (ISS module)")_ module and reconfigured a portion of the station in preparation for future assembly missions.[[NASA 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-presskit-3) STS-120 was flown by [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle")[_Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery"), and was the twenty-third Space Shuttle mission to the ISS. It was Discovery's 34th flight.

### Crew notes

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Exp16STS120commanders.jpg/250px-Exp16STS120commanders.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Exp16STS120commanders.jpg)

Two commanders: Melroy and Whitson place the STS-120 mission insignia on the wall of the newly installed _Harmony_ module.

As commander of STS-120, Pamela Melroy became the second woman (after [Eileen Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eileen_Collins "Eileen Collins")) to command a Space Shuttle mission.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-second-7) Additionally, the [Expedition 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_16 "Expedition 16") crew that received STS-120 was commanded by [Peggy Whitson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggy_Whitson "Peggy Whitson"), the first female ISS commander.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-space2-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fox2-9) The flight of STS-120 thus became the first time two female mission commanders were in space at the same time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-chicks-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-msnbc1-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-history1-12)

### _Harmony_ (Node 2)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Harmony (Node 2)")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/ISS_Node_2_module.jpg/250px-ISS_Node_2_module.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS_Node_2_module.jpg)

_Harmony_ under assembly at the SSPF

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/STS120Lightsaber.jpg/250px-STS120Lightsaber.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS120Lightsaber.jpg)

Astronaut [Jim Reilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_F._Reilly "James F. Reilly") helped welcome [R2-D2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R2-D2 "R2-D2") and [Luke Skywalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Skywalker "Luke Skywalker")'s [lightsaber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightsaber "Lightsaber") from _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ to the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center").

STS-120 delivered launch package 10A to the International Space Station (ISS).[[NASA 5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-harm1-14) It consisted of the U.S. _[Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony\_(ISS\_module) "Harmony (ISS module)")_ module (also known as Node 2), with four DC-to-DC Converter Unit (DDCU) racks and three Zero-g Storage Racks (ZSR) installed; a Power and Data Grapple Fixture (PDGF) for the station's robot arm, and a Shuttle Power Distribution Unit (SPDU). _Harmony_ was manufactured for NASA by [Thales Alenia Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Alenia_Space "Thales Alenia Space") in [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"), Italy, as part of an agreement between NASA and the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") and was the first pressurized habitable module delivered to the station since the [_Pirs_ docking compartment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirs_(ISS_module) "Pirs (ISS module)") was installed in August 2001.

Since STS-120 docked to the [Pressurized Mating Adapter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressurized_Mating_Adapter "Pressurized Mating Adapter")-2 (PMA-2) on the forward port of the _[Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny\_(ISS\_module) "Destiny (ISS module)")_ module, installation of _Harmony_ occurred in two stages: STS-120 installed _Harmony_ to the port node of the _Unity_ module. After _Discovery_ undocked, the [station's robotic arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm2 "Canadarm2") detached PMA-2 from _Destiny_, and moved it to the forward port of _Harmony_. Following the relocation of PMA-2, the robotic arm was used to move _Harmony_ from its initial position to its final position, on the forward port of _Destiny_.[[NASA 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-pma3-15)

The final positioning of _Harmony_ allowed for the later installation of the [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESA "ESA")_[Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus\_(ISS\_module) "Columbus (ISS module)")_ and [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA")_[Kibō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_Experiment\_Module "Japanese Experiment Module")_ research modules, which were attached to the side ports of _Harmony_.

### P6 relocation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: P6 relocation")]

During STS-120, the [P6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S6_truss "S6 truss") solar arrays were moved from the [Z1 truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z1_truss "Z1 truss") on top of _Unity_, to their final position at the port end of the truss.

### Outreach

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Outreach")]

STS-120 carried the signatures of over 500,000 students that participated in the 2007 Student Signatures in Space program, jointly sponsored by NASA and Lockheed Martin.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nwi-16)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-hobart-17) In celebration of Space Day in May 2007, students from over 500 schools around the world signed giant posters. Their signatures were scanned onto a disk, and the disk was manifested on the STS-120 mission.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-nwi-16)

Also during STS-120, the [lightsaber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightsaber "Lightsaber") used by actor [Mark Hamill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hamill "Mark Hamill") in the 1983 film _[Return of the Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_the\_Jedi "Return of the Jedi")_ was flown to the station and returned to Earth.[[NASA 7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-Whatsgoingup-18) Stowed on-board _Discovery_ for the length of the mission, the [prop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_property "Theatrical property") was flown in honor of the 30th anniversary of the _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ franchise.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19) On August 28, 2007, [Chewbacca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chewbacca "Chewbacca") from the _Star Wars_ films presented the lightsaber to NASA officials from [Space Center Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Center_Houston "Space Center Houston"), in an official ceremony at [Oakland International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_International_Airport "Oakland International Airport").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19) The lightsaber was then flown to Houston, where it was greeted by [Stormtroopers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_stormtrooper "Imperial stormtrooper"). The lightsaber will be displayed at Space Center Houston.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-saber-19)

## Mission background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mission background")]

At the time of the _[Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Columbia\_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster")_ disaster, STS-120 was scheduled for early 2004. It was delayed repeatedly until October 23, 2007.

NASA originally scheduled the launch for October 20, 2007, but due to the International Space Station program requirement, launch was delayed to October 23, 2007.[[NASA 8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-tv-20)

In light of the small gouge to the underside of _Endeavour_ that occurred on [STS-118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-118 "STS-118"), in August 2007, NASA managers announced that they expected to add a fifth spacewalk to the STS-120 mission, designed to test a heat-shield repair tool.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-goo-21) The repair technique was originally scheduled for a flight in 2008, but following STS-118, it was decided to move up the testing. The repair tool, called a [TPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_thermal_protection_system "Space Shuttle thermal protection system") (thermal protection system) repair [ablator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ablation "Ablation") dispenser (T-RAD), has never been tested in space, so the spacewalk would have allowed managers to evaluate its effectiveness in low gravity environments.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-eva5-22) During the course of the mission, issues with the [S4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Truss_Structure#P3/P4,_S3/S4_truss_assemblies "Integrated Truss Structure")[starboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboard "Starboard")[Solar Alpha Rotary Joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Alpha_Rotary_Joint "Solar Alpha Rotary Joint") (SARJ), and P6 Solar Array, deferred this test objective to a future mission.

The mission marked:[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-ql-5)

*   151st NASA crewed spaceflight
*   120th Space Shuttle flight since [STS-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-1 "STS-1")
*   34th flight of _[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_
*   95th post-_[Challenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Challenger\_disaster "Space Shuttle Challenger disaster")_ mission
*   7th post-_Columbia_ mission

### Launch preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=STS-120&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Launch preparations")]
