**George David "Zambo" Zamka** (born June 29, 1962) is a former [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps")[pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator "Naval aviator") with over 3500 flight hours in more than 30 different aircraft. Zamka piloted the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") in its October 2007 mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and served as the commander of mission [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130") in February 2010.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

George David Zamka was born on June 29, 1962, at Margaret Hague Hospital in [Jersey City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_City,_New_Jersey "Jersey City, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-2) He was raised in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); [Irvington, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvington,_New_York "Irvington, New York"); [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Colombia;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-Mom-3) and [Rochester Hills, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Hills,_Michigan "Rochester Hills, Michigan"). He graduated from [Rochester Adams High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Adams_High_School "Rochester Adams High School") in Michigan in 1980. His personal hobbies include weightlifting, running, bicycling, scuba diving, and boating.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-4)

Zamka is married and has two children. His extended family resides in Colorado, Mississippi, Georgia, Indiana, Florida and Tennessee. Zamka is of [Colombian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_people "Colombian people")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-6) and [Polish ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American "Polish American").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-rhg-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-9)

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Zamka graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") from the [United States Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy "United States Naval Academy") in 1984. He was then commissioned as a second lieutenant in the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). He received [A-6E Intruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-6_Intruder "A-6 Intruder") training at [Naval Air Station Whidbey Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whidbey_Island "Naval Air Station Whidbey Island"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") in 1985–1987. He was assigned to [VMA(AW)-242](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMA(AW)-242 "VMA(AW)-242") at [Marine Corps Air Station El Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_El_Toro "Marine Corps Air Station El Toro"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). In addition to flight safety and administration, he was a squadron weapons and tactics instructor. In 1990, he trained as an [F/A-18D Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18 "F/A-18") pilot and was then assigned to [VMFA(AW)-121](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMFA(AW)-121 "VMFA(AW)-121"). Zamka flew 66 combat missions during [Operation Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm "Operation Desert Storm"). In 1993, he was assigned to the [1st Battalion, 5th Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Battalion,_5th_Marines "1st Battalion, 5th Marines") at [Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Base_Camp_Pendleton "Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton"), California as a [forward air controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_air_controller "Forward air controller"). In December 1994, he graduated from the [U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School"), following which, he served as an [F/A-18 Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18_Hornet "F/A-18 Hornet") test pilot and operations officer.

In 1997, he earned a Masters of Science degree in engineering management from the [Florida Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Institute_of_Technology "Florida Institute of Technology"). In 1998, he returned to VMFA(AW)-121 and deployed to [MCAS Iwakuni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCAS_Iwakuni "MCAS Iwakuni"), Japan.

In August 2010, Zamka retired from the Marine Corps after almost 30 years of distinguished service. During his time as a pilot for the Marine Corps, Zamka logged more than 5,000 flight hours spanning 30 different aircraft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)As of May 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit) he is [chairman of the board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_board "Chairman of the board") of the [National Association of Spaceports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Spaceports?action=edit&redlink=1 "National Association of Spaceports (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-11)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

In June 1998, Zamka was selected for the NASA astronaut program, and reported for training in August. He served as lead for the Shuttle training and procedures division and as supervisor for the astronaut candidate class of 2004. Zamka made his first spaceflight as the pilot of mission STS-120, and second as the commander for [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130"). In March 2013, Zamka decided to retire from NASA.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-12)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1) In the two shuttle missions Zamka completed, he logged more than 692 hours in space and travelled 12 million miles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)

## Honors and awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honors and awards")]

Zamka has received the following honors and awards: the [Legion of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Merit "Legion of Merit"), [Distinguished Flying Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States) "Distinguished Flying Cross (United States)"), [Defense Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Meritorious_Service_Medal "Defense Meritorious Service Medal"), [Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meritorious_Service_Medal_(United_States) "Meritorious Service Medal (United States)"), [Navy Strike Air Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Medal "Air Medal") (6), [Navy Commendation Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Commendation_Medal "Navy Commendation Medal") with [Combat "V"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_%22V%22 "Combat \"V\""), and various other military service and campaign awards. Distinguished Graduate, U.S. Naval Academy. Commodore's list and Academic Achievement Award, Training Air Wing Five. Recipient of the [NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Outstanding_Leadership_Medal "NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal"), two [NASA Space Flight Medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Space_Flight_Medal "NASA Space Flight Medal"), four NASA Superior Accomplishment Awards and the GEM Award. He received also Officer's Cross of the [Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Republic_of_Poland "Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland") (2010).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-14)

## Promotional activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotional activities")]

In March 2008, Zamka visited Colombia's [Planetarium of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Planetarium of Bogotá") with the crew of mission STS-120 to share their experience as NASA astronauts with 200 students, 50 teachers, and 20 science major experts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-15)

**George David "Zambo" Zamka** (born June 29, 1962) is a former [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps")[pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator "Naval aviator") with over 3500 flight hours in more than 30 different aircraft. Zamka piloted the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") in its October 2007 mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and served as the commander of mission [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130") in February 2010.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

George David Zamka was born on June 29, 1962, at Margaret Hague Hospital in [Jersey City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_City,_New_Jersey "Jersey City, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-2) He was raised in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); [Irvington, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvington,_New_York "Irvington, New York"); [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Colombia;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-Mom-3) and [Rochester Hills, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Hills,_Michigan "Rochester Hills, Michigan"). He graduated from [Rochester Adams High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Adams_High_School "Rochester Adams High School") in Michigan in 1980. His personal hobbies include weightlifting, running, bicycling, scuba diving, and boating.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-4)

Zamka is married and has two children. His extended family resides in Colorado, Mississippi, Georgia, Indiana, Florida and Tennessee. Zamka is of [Colombian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_people "Colombian people")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-6) and [Polish ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American "Polish American").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-rhg-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-9)

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Zamka graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") from the [United States Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy "United States Naval Academy") in 1984. He was then commissioned as a second lieutenant in the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). He received [A-6E Intruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-6_Intruder "A-6 Intruder") training at [Naval Air Station Whidbey Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whidbey_Island "Naval Air Station Whidbey Island"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") in 1985–1987. He was assigned to [VMA(AW)-242](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMA(AW)-242 "VMA(AW)-242") at [Marine Corps Air Station El Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_El_Toro "Marine Corps Air Station El Toro"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). In addition to flight safety and administration, he was a squadron weapons and tactics instructor. In 1990, he trained as an [F/A-18D Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18 "F/A-18") pilot and was then assigned to [VMFA(AW)-121](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMFA(AW)-121 "VMFA(AW)-121"). Zamka flew 66 combat missions during [Operation Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm "Operation Desert Storm"). In 1993, he was assigned to the [1st Battalion, 5th Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Battalion,_5th_Marines "1st Battalion, 5th Marines") at [Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Base_Camp_Pendleton "Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton"), California as a [forward air controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_air_controller "Forward air controller"). In December 1994, he graduated from the [U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School"), following which, he served as an [F/A-18 Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18_Hornet "F/A-18 Hornet") test pilot and operations officer.

In 1997, he earned a Masters of Science degree in engineering management from the [Florida Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Institute_of_Technology "Florida Institute of Technology"). In 1998, he returned to VMFA(AW)-121 and deployed to [MCAS Iwakuni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCAS_Iwakuni "MCAS Iwakuni"), Japan.

In August 2010, Zamka retired from the Marine Corps after almost 30 years of distinguished service. During his time as a pilot for the Marine Corps, Zamka logged more than 5,000 flight hours spanning 30 different aircraft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)As of May 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit) he is [chairman of the board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_board "Chairman of the board") of the [National Association of Spaceports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Spaceports?action=edit&redlink=1 "National Association of Spaceports (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-11)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

In June 1998, Zamka was selected for the NASA astronaut program, and reported for training in August. He served as lead for the Shuttle training and procedures division and as supervisor for the astronaut candidate class of 2004. Zamka made his first spaceflight as the pilot of mission STS-120, and second as the commander for [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130"). In March 2013, Zamka decided to retire from NASA.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-12)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1) In the two shuttle missions Zamka completed, he logged more than 692 hours in space and travelled 12 million miles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)

## Honors and awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honors and awards")]

Zamka has received the following honors and awards: the [Legion of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Merit "Legion of Merit"), [Distinguished Flying Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States) "Distinguished Flying Cross (United States)"), [Defense Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Meritorious_Service_Medal "Defense Meritorious Service Medal"), [Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meritorious_Service_Medal_(United_States) "Meritorious Service Medal (United States)"), [Navy Strike Air Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Medal "Air Medal") (6), [Navy Commendation Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Commendation_Medal "Navy Commendation Medal") with [Combat "V"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_%22V%22 "Combat \"V\""), and various other military service and campaign awards. Distinguished Graduate, U.S. Naval Academy. Commodore's list and Academic Achievement Award, Training Air Wing Five. Recipient of the [NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Outstanding_Leadership_Medal "NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal"), two [NASA Space Flight Medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Space_Flight_Medal "NASA Space Flight Medal"), four NASA Superior Accomplishment Awards and the GEM Award. He received also Officer's Cross of the [Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Republic_of_Poland "Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland") (2010).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-14)

## Promotional activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotional activities")]

In March 2008, Zamka visited Colombia's [Planetarium of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Planetarium of Bogotá") with the crew of mission STS-120 to share their experience as NASA astronauts with 200 students, 50 teachers, and 20 science major experts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Zamka#cite_note-15)

**Douglas Harry Wheelock** (born May 5, 1960) is an American [engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineer "Engineer") and [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut"). He has flown in space twice, logging 178 days on the [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle"), [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"), and Russian [Soyuz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_(spacecraft) "Soyuz (spacecraft)"). On July 12, 2011, Wheelock announced that he would be returning to active duty with the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") in support of [Operation Enduring Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Enduring_Freedom "Operation Enduring Freedom").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-3) He is currently working with [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") to test the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_spacecraft "Orion spacecraft") at the [Glenn Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Research_Center "Glenn Research Center") in Plum Brook, Ohio.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-magill-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Douglas Wheelock was born in [Binghamton, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binghamton,_New_York "Binghamton, New York"), to Olin and Margaret Wheelock. In a pre-flight interview, Wheelock stated that he was inspired to become an astronaut at an early age. He also stated that a major turning point in his life was the [Apollo 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") Moon landing in July 1969.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-preflight-5) In 1978 Wheelock graduated from Windsor Central High School in [Windsor, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_(town),_New_York "Windsor (town), New York"), before attending the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") at [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point,_New_York "West Point, New York").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6) He earned a Master of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering at [Georgia Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Institute_of_Technology "Georgia Institute of Technology") in 1992.

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Wheelock spent four years as a cadet at West Point, graduating in the class of 1983 with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [applied science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_science "Applied science") and [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"). After graduation he was commissioned a [second lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant "Second lieutenant") in the U.S. Army's [Infantry Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infantry_Branch_(United_States) "Infantry Branch (United States)") and entered flight school the next year. In September 1984, then Lieutenant Wheelock graduated at the top of his flight class and was designated an [army aviator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Aviator_Badge "United States Aviator Badge"). He subsequently served in the Pacific as a combat aviation section leader, platoon leader, company executive officer, battalion operations officer, and commander of an air cavalry troop in the [9th Cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Cavalry_Regiment_(United_States) "9th Cavalry Regiment (United States)"). He was later assigned to the Aviation Directorate of Combat Developments as an advanced weapons research and development engineer.

Wheelock was selected as a member of Class 104 at the [U.S. Naval Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Naval_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Naval Test Pilot School") and upon completion was assigned as an experimental test pilot with the Army Aviation Technical Test Center (ATTC). His flight testing was focused in the areas of tactical reconnaissance and surveillance systems in the [OH-58D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OH-58D "OH-58D"), [UH-60](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UH-60 "UH-60"), [RU-21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RU-21 "RU-21") and [C-23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-23_Sherpa "C-23 Sherpa") aircraft. He served as division chief for fixed-wing testing of airborne signal and imagery intelligence systems in support of the National Program Office for Intelligence and Electronic Warfare.

While on active duty, Wheelock received a [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") degree in [aerospace engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerospace_engineering "Aerospace engineering") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech "Georgia Tech") in 1992. In August 1996 Wheelock was assigned to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") as a Space Shuttle integration test engineer. His technical duties involved engineering liaison for launch and landing operations of the Space Shuttle. He was selected as the vehicle integration test team lead for the joint Space Shuttle and Russian Space Station _[Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir "Mir")_ mission [STS-86](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-86 "STS-86"), and lead engineer for International Space Station hardware fit checks.

Wheelock is a graduate of the Army Airborne and Air Assault Courses, the Infantry and Aviation Officer Advanced Courses, the Combined Arms Services Staff School, the Material Acquisition Management Course, and the [U.S. Army Command and General Staff College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army_Command_and_General_Staff_College "U.S. Army Command and General Staff College"). In July 2011, Wheelock left for a tour of duty in support of Operation Enduring Freedom. A dual-rated master army aviator astronaut, he has logged over 2,500 flight hours in 43 different rotary and fixed-wing aircraft.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg/250px-Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg)

Wheelock's astronaut candidate photo

In August 1998 Wheelock reported for [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronaut candidate training. Having completed the initial two years of intensive Space Shuttle and Space Station training, he was assigned to the Astronaut Office ISS Operations Branch as a Russian Liaison, participating in the testing and integration of Russian hardware and software products developed for the ISS. He worked extensively with the Energia Aerospace Company in [Moscow, Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow,_Russia "Moscow, Russia"), developing and verifying dual-language procedures for ISS crews. Wheelock led joint U.S./Russian teams to the [Baikonur Cosmodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baikonur_Cosmodrome "Baikonur Cosmodrome") in [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan") to oversee bench reviews, inventory, loading and launch of the first four uncrewed ISS resupply capsules.

In 2001, Wheelock assumed duties as the crew support astronaut for the ISS [Expedition 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_2 "Expedition 2") crew, which was in orbit for 147 days from March 2001 to August 2001, and for the ISS [Expedition 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_4 "Expedition 4") crew, which was on orbit for 195 days from December 2001 to June 2002. He was the primary contact for all crew needs, coordination, planning and interactions, and was the primary representative of the crews while they were in orbit. In August 2002, Wheelock was assigned as a spacecraft communicator ([CAPCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_controller#Spacecraft_communicator_(CAPCOM) "Flight controller")) in the Mission Control Center in [Houston, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston,_Texas "Houston, Texas"). In this role, he was the primary communication link between crews in orbit and the ground support team in the Control Center. His work as a CAPCOM culminated in his assignment as the lead CAPCOM for the ISS [Expedition 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_8 "Expedition 8") mission, which was 194 days in duration.

In July 2004, Wheelock served as an [aquanaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquanaut "Aquanaut") during the [NEEMO 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEEMO#NEEMO_6:_July_12%E2%80%9321,_2004 "NEEMO") mission aboard the [Aquarius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquarius_(laboratory) "Aquarius (laboratory)")[underwater laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underwater_habitat "Underwater habitat"), living and working underwater for ten days.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-six-7)

In January 2005 and again in 2016, he was assigned as NASA's Director of Operations – Russia where he served at the [Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gagarin_Cosmonaut_Training_Center "Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center") in [Star City, Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_City,_Russia "Star City, Russia"). He was responsible for supporting Russia-based training, logistic, and administrative needs of NASA astronauts preparing for flight on the ISS. Wheelock was the primary liaison between Star City and NASA operations in Houston, including medical, training, science, contracting, public affairs, and administration departments. He was also responsible for liaison duties between NASA and the [Russian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Space_Agency "Russian Space Agency"), as well as the Russian aerospace industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6)

After his first spaceflight, Wheelock was assigned as the backup to [T.J. Creamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Creamer "Timothy Creamer") for the [Soyuz TMA-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-17 "Soyuz TMA-17")/[Expedition 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_22 "Expedition 22")/[Expedition 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_23 "Expedition 23") mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"). Creamer completed a successful 163-day mission from 2009 to 2010.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-8)

As of September 2019, Wheelock was working as an astronaut trainer testing systems aboard the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_spacecraft "Orion spacecraft").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-magill-4) That month, he contributed to an article in _[The Columbus Dispatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Columbus\_Dispatch "The Columbus Dispatch")_ detailing the inaccuracies of the space science fiction film _[Ad Astra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad\_Astra\_(film) "Ad Astra (film)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-burger-9)

### Spaceflight experience

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spaceflight experience")]

#### STS-120

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: STS-120")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg/250px-Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg)

Wheelock working on the outside of the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") during STS-120

On October 23, 2007, Wheelock launched on his first spaceflight aboard [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery"). During the STS-120 mission, Wheelock was [Mission Specialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Specialist "Mission Specialist") 3 on a multinational crew whose mission was to deliver the [Node 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_2 "Node 2") module to the International Space Station. Wheelock participated in three [spacewalks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacewalks "Spacewalks") with fellow astronaut [Scott Parazynski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Parazynski "Scott Parazynski") in order to perform mission critical tasks on the exterior of the Station. The spacewalks involved outfitting the Node 2 module, storing an S-band antenna, work on the [Integrated Truss Structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Truss_Structure "Integrated Truss Structure"), and [External Stowage Platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_Stowage_Platform "External Stowage Platform") 2. During the mission a solar array on the P6 truss tore requiring an emergency repair by Wheelock and Parazynski. Parazynski attached cufflinks to the solar array allowing it to expand without additional damage. Wheelock orbited the Earth 238 times during the 15-day mission.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-10)

#### Expedition 24/25

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Expedition 24/25")]

Wheelock launched to the International Space Station on June 15, 2010, aboard the [Soyuz TMA-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-19 "Soyuz TMA-19") spacecraft with [Fyodor Yurchikhin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fyodor_Yurchikhin "Fyodor Yurchikhin") and [Shannon Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Walker "Shannon Walker").

Wheelock joined the [Expedition 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_24 "Expedition 24") crew in progress.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-Hires24-11) During the mission he participated in several scientific investigations. On July 31, 2010, a pump module on the exterior of the Space Station failed. Wheelock and [Tracy Caldwell-Dyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Caldwell-Dyson "Tracy Caldwell-Dyson") made three spacewalks to replace the module, during which he sustained long-term damage to his vision.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-AmmoniaPump-12)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-burger-9) The failed pump module was later returned home on [STS-135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-135 "STS-135").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-13)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_%28closeup%29.jpg/250px-Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_%28closeup%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_(closeup).jpg)

Wheelock and his crewmates outside their Soyuz spacecraft

On September 22, 2010, Wheelock took command of the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") at the beginning of [Expedition 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_25 "Expedition 25").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-14) He is the first U.S. Army officer to command the ISS.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-15) Wheelock and his crew continued science and maintenance of the space station. Wheelock is sharing pictures of the Earth, station and views of space via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), as [Soichi Noguchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soichi_Noguchi "Soichi Noguchi") did before him.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-16) In September 2010, Wheelock tweeted photos from space of [Hurricane Earl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Earl_(2010) "Hurricane Earl (2010)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-New_York_Daily_News-17) He also participated in a [NASA Tweetup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Tweetup "NASA Tweetup") on March 16, 2011.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-18)

He became the first person to "check in" from space on October 22, using the mobile social networking application [Foursquare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foursquare_City_Guide "Foursquare City Guide"). Wheelock's check-in to the International Space Station launched a partnership between NASA and Foursquare to connect its users to the space agency, enabling them to explore the universe and discover Earth.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-NASA-19)

He returned to Earth on November 26, 2010, aboard the Soyuz.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

His hometown is Windsor, New York. Wheelock's parents, Olin and Margaret Wheelock, reside in upstate New York.

In 1989 he was selected by the U.S. [Jaycees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaycees "Jaycees") as one of "Ten Outstanding Young Men of America". In 1990 the [Veterans of Foreign Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterans_of_Foreign_Wars "Veterans of Foreign Wars") selected Wheelock as an "Outstanding Spokesman for Freedom".

### Organizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Organizations")]

Wheelock is a member of the [Society of Experimental Test Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Experimental_Test_Pilots "Society of Experimental Test Pilots"), the [Society of American Military Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_American_Military_Engineers "Society of American Military Engineers"), the [Association of the United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_the_United_States_Army "Association of the United States Army"), and the [Army Aviation Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Aviation_Association_of_America?action=edit&redlink=1 "Army Aviation Association of America (page does not exist)").

**Douglas Harry Wheelock** (born May 5, 1960) is an American [engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineer "Engineer") and [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut"). He has flown in space twice, logging 178 days on the [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle"), [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"), and Russian [Soyuz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_(spacecraft) "Soyuz (spacecraft)"). On July 12, 2011, Wheelock announced that he would be returning to active duty with the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") in support of [Operation Enduring Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Enduring_Freedom "Operation Enduring Freedom").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-3) He is currently working with [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") to test the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_spacecraft "Orion spacecraft") at the [Glenn Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Research_Center "Glenn Research Center") in Plum Brook, Ohio.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-magill-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Douglas Wheelock was born in [Binghamton, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binghamton,_New_York "Binghamton, New York"), to Olin and Margaret Wheelock. In a pre-flight interview, Wheelock stated that he was inspired to become an astronaut at an early age. He also stated that a major turning point in his life was the [Apollo 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") Moon landing in July 1969.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-preflight-5) In 1978 Wheelock graduated from Windsor Central High School in [Windsor, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_(town),_New_York "Windsor (town), New York"), before attending the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") at [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point,_New_York "West Point, New York").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6) He earned a Master of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering at [Georgia Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Institute_of_Technology "Georgia Institute of Technology") in 1992.

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Wheelock spent four years as a cadet at West Point, graduating in the class of 1983 with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [applied science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_science "Applied science") and [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"). After graduation he was commissioned a [second lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant "Second lieutenant") in the U.S. Army's [Infantry Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infantry_Branch_(United_States) "Infantry Branch (United States)") and entered flight school the next year. In September 1984, then Lieutenant Wheelock graduated at the top of his flight class and was designated an [army aviator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Aviator_Badge "United States Aviator Badge"). He subsequently served in the Pacific as a combat aviation section leader, platoon leader, company executive officer, battalion operations officer, and commander of an air cavalry troop in the [9th Cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Cavalry_Regiment_(United_States) "9th Cavalry Regiment (United States)"). He was later assigned to the Aviation Directorate of Combat Developments as an advanced weapons research and development engineer.

Wheelock was selected as a member of Class 104 at the [U.S. Naval Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Naval_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Naval Test Pilot School") and upon completion was assigned as an experimental test pilot with the Army Aviation Technical Test Center (ATTC). His flight testing was focused in the areas of tactical reconnaissance and surveillance systems in the [OH-58D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OH-58D "OH-58D"), [UH-60](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UH-60 "UH-60"), [RU-21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RU-21 "RU-21") and [C-23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-23_Sherpa "C-23 Sherpa") aircraft. He served as division chief for fixed-wing testing of airborne signal and imagery intelligence systems in support of the National Program Office for Intelligence and Electronic Warfare.

While on active duty, Wheelock received a [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") degree in [aerospace engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerospace_engineering "Aerospace engineering") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech "Georgia Tech") in 1992. In August 1996 Wheelock was assigned to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") as a Space Shuttle integration test engineer. His technical duties involved engineering liaison for launch and landing operations of the Space Shuttle. He was selected as the vehicle integration test team lead for the joint Space Shuttle and Russian Space Station _[Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir "Mir")_ mission [STS-86](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-86 "STS-86"), and lead engineer for International Space Station hardware fit checks.

Wheelock is a graduate of the Army Airborne and Air Assault Courses, the Infantry and Aviation Officer Advanced Courses, the Combined Arms Services Staff School, the Material Acquisition Management Course, and the [U.S. Army Command and General Staff College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army_Command_and_General_Staff_College "U.S. Army Command and General Staff College"). In July 2011, Wheelock left for a tour of duty in support of Operation Enduring Freedom. A dual-rated master army aviator astronaut, he has logged over 2,500 flight hours in 43 different rotary and fixed-wing aircraft.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg/250px-Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douglas_H._Wheelock.jpg)

Wheelock's astronaut candidate photo

In August 1998 Wheelock reported for [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronaut candidate training. Having completed the initial two years of intensive Space Shuttle and Space Station training, he was assigned to the Astronaut Office ISS Operations Branch as a Russian Liaison, participating in the testing and integration of Russian hardware and software products developed for the ISS. He worked extensively with the Energia Aerospace Company in [Moscow, Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow,_Russia "Moscow, Russia"), developing and verifying dual-language procedures for ISS crews. Wheelock led joint U.S./Russian teams to the [Baikonur Cosmodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baikonur_Cosmodrome "Baikonur Cosmodrome") in [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan") to oversee bench reviews, inventory, loading and launch of the first four uncrewed ISS resupply capsules.

In 2001, Wheelock assumed duties as the crew support astronaut for the ISS [Expedition 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_2 "Expedition 2") crew, which was in orbit for 147 days from March 2001 to August 2001, and for the ISS [Expedition 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_4 "Expedition 4") crew, which was on orbit for 195 days from December 2001 to June 2002. He was the primary contact for all crew needs, coordination, planning and interactions, and was the primary representative of the crews while they were in orbit. In August 2002, Wheelock was assigned as a spacecraft communicator ([CAPCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_controller#Spacecraft_communicator_(CAPCOM) "Flight controller")) in the Mission Control Center in [Houston, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston,_Texas "Houston, Texas"). In this role, he was the primary communication link between crews in orbit and the ground support team in the Control Center. His work as a CAPCOM culminated in his assignment as the lead CAPCOM for the ISS [Expedition 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_8 "Expedition 8") mission, which was 194 days in duration.

In July 2004, Wheelock served as an [aquanaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquanaut "Aquanaut") during the [NEEMO 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEEMO#NEEMO_6:_July_12%E2%80%9321,_2004 "NEEMO") mission aboard the [Aquarius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquarius_(laboratory) "Aquarius (laboratory)")[underwater laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underwater_habitat "Underwater habitat"), living and working underwater for ten days.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-six-7)

In January 2005 and again in 2016, he was assigned as NASA's Director of Operations – Russia where he served at the [Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gagarin_Cosmonaut_Training_Center "Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center") in [Star City, Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_City,_Russia "Star City, Russia"). He was responsible for supporting Russia-based training, logistic, and administrative needs of NASA astronauts preparing for flight on the ISS. Wheelock was the primary liaison between Star City and NASA operations in Houston, including medical, training, science, contracting, public affairs, and administration departments. He was also responsible for liaison duties between NASA and the [Russian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Space_Agency "Russian Space Agency"), as well as the Russian aerospace industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-bio-6)

After his first spaceflight, Wheelock was assigned as the backup to [T.J. Creamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Creamer "Timothy Creamer") for the [Soyuz TMA-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-17 "Soyuz TMA-17")/[Expedition 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_22 "Expedition 22")/[Expedition 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_23 "Expedition 23") mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"). Creamer completed a successful 163-day mission from 2009 to 2010.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-8)

As of September 2019, Wheelock was working as an astronaut trainer testing systems aboard the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_spacecraft "Orion spacecraft").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-magill-4) That month, he contributed to an article in _[The Columbus Dispatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Columbus\_Dispatch "The Columbus Dispatch")_ detailing the inaccuracies of the space science fiction film _[Ad Astra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad\_Astra\_(film) "Ad Astra (film)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-burger-9)

### Spaceflight experience

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spaceflight experience")]

#### STS-120

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: STS-120")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg/250px-Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Doug_Wheelock-STS-120.jpg)

Wheelock working on the outside of the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") during STS-120

On October 23, 2007, Wheelock launched on his first spaceflight aboard [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery"). During the STS-120 mission, Wheelock was [Mission Specialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Specialist "Mission Specialist") 3 on a multinational crew whose mission was to deliver the [Node 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_2 "Node 2") module to the International Space Station. Wheelock participated in three [spacewalks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacewalks "Spacewalks") with fellow astronaut [Scott Parazynski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Parazynski "Scott Parazynski") in order to perform mission critical tasks on the exterior of the Station. The spacewalks involved outfitting the Node 2 module, storing an S-band antenna, work on the [Integrated Truss Structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Truss_Structure "Integrated Truss Structure"), and [External Stowage Platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_Stowage_Platform "External Stowage Platform") 2. During the mission a solar array on the P6 truss tore requiring an emergency repair by Wheelock and Parazynski. Parazynski attached cufflinks to the solar array allowing it to expand without additional damage. Wheelock orbited the Earth 238 times during the 15-day mission.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-10)

#### Expedition 24/25

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Expedition 24/25")]

Wheelock launched to the International Space Station on June 15, 2010, aboard the [Soyuz TMA-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-19 "Soyuz TMA-19") spacecraft with [Fyodor Yurchikhin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fyodor_Yurchikhin "Fyodor Yurchikhin") and [Shannon Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Walker "Shannon Walker").

Wheelock joined the [Expedition 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_24 "Expedition 24") crew in progress.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-Hires24-11) During the mission he participated in several scientific investigations. On July 31, 2010, a pump module on the exterior of the Space Station failed. Wheelock and [Tracy Caldwell-Dyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Caldwell-Dyson "Tracy Caldwell-Dyson") made three spacewalks to replace the module, during which he sustained long-term damage to his vision.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-AmmoniaPump-12)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-burger-9) The failed pump module was later returned home on [STS-135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-135 "STS-135").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-13)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_%28closeup%29.jpg/250px-Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_%28closeup%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soyuz_TMA-19_Crew_in_front_of_the_capsule_(closeup).jpg)

Wheelock and his crewmates outside their Soyuz spacecraft

On September 22, 2010, Wheelock took command of the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") at the beginning of [Expedition 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_25 "Expedition 25").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-14) He is the first U.S. Army officer to command the ISS.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-15) Wheelock and his crew continued science and maintenance of the space station. Wheelock is sharing pictures of the Earth, station and views of space via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), as [Soichi Noguchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soichi_Noguchi "Soichi Noguchi") did before him.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-16) In September 2010, Wheelock tweeted photos from space of [Hurricane Earl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Earl_(2010) "Hurricane Earl (2010)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-New_York_Daily_News-17) He also participated in a [NASA Tweetup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Tweetup "NASA Tweetup") on March 16, 2011.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-18)

He became the first person to "check in" from space on October 22, using the mobile social networking application [Foursquare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foursquare_City_Guide "Foursquare City Guide"). Wheelock's check-in to the International Space Station launched a partnership between NASA and Foursquare to connect its users to the space agency, enabling them to explore the universe and discover Earth.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_H._Wheelock#cite_note-NASA-19)

He returned to Earth on November 26, 2010, aboard the Soyuz.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

His hometown is Windsor, New York. Wheelock's parents, Olin and Margaret Wheelock, reside in upstate New York.

In 1989 he was selected by the U.S. [Jaycees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaycees "Jaycees") as one of "Ten Outstanding Young Men of America". In 1990 the [Veterans of Foreign Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterans_of_Foreign_Wars "Veterans of Foreign Wars") selected Wheelock as an "Outstanding Spokesman for Freedom".

### Organizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douglas_H._Wheelock&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Organizations")]

Wheelock is a member of the [Society of Experimental Test Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Experimental_Test_Pilots "Society of Experimental Test Pilots"), the [Society of American Military Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_American_Military_Engineers "Society of American Military Engineers"), the [Association of the United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_the_United_States_Army "Association of the United States Army"), and the [Army Aviation Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Aviation_Association_of_America?action=edit&redlink=1 "Army Aviation Association of America (page does not exist)").

Major **Paolo Angelo Nespoli** (born 6 April 1957) is an Italian [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineer "Engineer") of the European Space Agency (ESA). In 2007, he first traveled into space aboard the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") as a mission specialist of STS-120. In December 2010 he again traveled into space aboard the [Soyuz TMA-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-20 "Soyuz TMA-20") spacecraft as an [Expedition 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_26 "Expedition 26")/[27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_27 "Expedition 27")[flight engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_engineer "Flight engineer"). Nespoli's third spaceflight was on board [Soyuz MS-05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_MS-05 "Soyuz MS-05"), which launched in July 2017 for [Expedition 52](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_52 "Expedition 52")/[53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_53 "Expedition 53"). He was also the European Space Agency's oldest active astronaut prior to his retirement in 2019.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

Nespoli's hometown is [Verano Brianza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verano_Brianza "Verano Brianza"), in northern Italy. He is married to Russian[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-2) Alexandra Ryabova, and they have one daughter and a son. Nespoli enjoys Scuba diving, piloting aircraft, photography, and building electronic equipment and computer software.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-3) He supports [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") team [Inter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-4)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Education")]

He received his bachelor's degree in Aerospace engineering in 1988 and his master's degree in 1989 in Aeronautics and Astronautics from [Polytechnic University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polytechnic_Institute_of_New_York_University "Polytechnic Institute of New York University") in New York.

He is a professional engineer, a private pilot, an advanced [scuba diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuba_diver "Scuba diver"), and a [nitrox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrox "Nitrox") diver. Due to his military background, he is also a master parachutist, parachute instructor, jump master, high altitude low opening and [Special Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Forces "Special Forces") operator in the [9th Paratroopers Assault Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Paratroopers_Assault_Regiment "9th Paratroopers Assault Regiment"). He joined the [Italian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Army "Italian Army") in 1977.

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Awards")]

Nespoli has received the following awards:

*   2007 [NASA Space Flight Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Space_Flight_Medal "NASA Space Flight Medal")
*   2007 Commendatore [Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic "Order of Merit of the Italian Republic")
*   2009 Cavaliere dell'[Ordine della Stella della solidarietà italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordine_della_Stella_della_solidariet%C3%A0_italiana "Ordine della Stella della solidarietà italiana")
*   2015 _America Award_ of the [Italy-USA Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy-USA_Foundation "Italy-USA Foundation")

## Astronaut career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Astronaut career")]

In July 1998, he was selected as an astronaut for [Italian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Space_Agency "Italian Space Agency") (ASI) and in August 1998, Nespoli was assigned by the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") to train at NASA's [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas").

In 2013, Nespoli served as cavenaut into the [ESA CAVES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESA_CAVES "ESA CAVES")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-5) training in [Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardinia "Sardinia"), alongside [Jeremy Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Hansen "Jeremy Hansen"), [Michael Barratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Barratt_(astronaut) "Michael Barratt (astronaut)"), [Jack Fisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_D._Fischer "Jack D. Fischer"), [Aleksei Ovchinin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksey_Ovchinin "Aleksey Ovchinin") and [Satoshi Furukawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoshi_Furukawa "Satoshi Furukawa").

### STS-120

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: STS-120")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/S120e006445.jpg/250px-S120e006445.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:S120e006445.jpg)

STS-120 mission specialist Paolo Nespoli in the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station")

On 23 October 2007 Paolo launched on board STS-120 to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"); the [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") mission which delivered the _[Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony\_Module "Harmony Module")_ module (formerly known as Node 2) to the International Space Station. _Harmony_ was built by [Thales Alenia Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Alenia_Space "Thales Alenia Space") at its facility in [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"). He participated as a mission specialist and remained in space for 15 days, 2 hours and 23 minutes. During STS-120, he participated in the Esperia mission for the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-6)

### Expedition 26/27 'MagISStra'

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Expedition 26/27 'MagISStra'")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/ISS-26_Paolo_Nespoli_with_Robonaut2.jpg/250px-ISS-26_Paolo_Nespoli_with_Robonaut2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS-26_Paolo_Nespoli_with_Robonaut2.jpg)

Expedition 26/27 flight engineer Paolo Nespoli poses with [Robonaut 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robonaut_2 "Robonaut 2").

Paolo Nespoli served as first flight engineer for [Expedition 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_26 "Expedition 26")/[27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_27 "Expedition 27"), Europe's third six-month mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-7)

On 15 December 2010 Nespoli flew aboard the [Soyuz TMA-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-20 "Soyuz TMA-20") spacecraft from [Baikonur Cosmodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baikonur_Cosmodrome "Baikonur Cosmodrome") in [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan") to the International Space Station with the Russian cosmonaut [Dmitri Kondratyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitri_Kondratyev "Dmitri Kondratyev") and NASA's astronaut [Catherine Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Coleman "Catherine Coleman"). The three members of the crew returned to Earth on 24 May 2011. This mission, dubbed ‘MagISStra’, is Paolo Nespoli's second flight in space.

From 15 December 2010 to 24 May 2011, Paolo Nespoli's duties[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-MagISStra-8) aboard the ISS included participating in the docking operations to receive Europe's second [Automated Transfer Vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_Transfer_Vehicle "Automated Transfer Vehicle") (ATV-2) _Johannes Kepler_, a visiting spacecraft that will deliver essential cargo to the Station.

In early January, Nespoli filmed the majority of the footage for the 2011 documentary film _[First Orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Orbit "First Orbit")_, and as a result is credited as its [director of photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer").

Nespoli took part in the arrival of the second Japanese HII Transfer Vehicle ([HTV-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H-II_Transfer_Vehicle "H-II Transfer Vehicle")), an uncrewed spacecraft used to resupply the ISS. He was the prime operator for berthing the HTV-2 to the ISS after the free-flying vehicle was captured by NASA astronaut Catherine Coleman. In May 2011, [Space Shuttle _Endeavour_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Endeavour "Space Shuttle Endeavour") has delivered the [Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Magnetic_Spectrometer "Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer") (AMS-02) to the ISS.

During Nespoli's stint with Expedition 27, his mother, Maria, died on 4 May 2011. The crew observed 1 minute of silence the following day around the time of her funeral.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-9)

Paolo Nespoli carried out an intensive programme of experiments in the Station, ranging from radiation monitoring to measurements that could improve [oil recovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum_extraction "Petroleum extraction") in petroleum reservoirs. The mission scientific programme covered different fields on human research, fluid physics, radiation, biology and technology demonstrations.

Nespoli contributed to the scientific exploitation of Europe's _Columbus_ laboratory. As an astronaut, he carried out several experiments for ESA, NASA and also the Japanese and Canadian space agencies. During the mission, Paolo participated in some educational activities: the educational programme ["Mission X: Train Like an Astronaut"](http://trainlikeanastronaut.org/) which gave children the chance to follow an international initiative built around health, well-being and nutrition. He also participated in a greenhouse activity in space. Nespoli used ESA's novel 3D camera to show images of the ISS.

As Paolo left the ISS on 23 May 2011 in the [Soyuz TMA-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-20 "Soyuz TMA-20") he was able to take the first pictures of a Space Shuttle docked with the ISS from the perspective of a Russian [Soyuz spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_spacecraft "Soyuz spacecraft").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-10)

### Expedition 52/53 and the VITA mission

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Expedition 52/53 and the VITA mission")]

Nespoli was part of Expedition 52/53, which started in 2017. He launched on [Soyuz MS-05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_MS-05 "Soyuz MS-05") on 28 July 2017 15:41 UTC.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-sfi-20170728-11) Nespoli's mission to the ISS was called **VITA**. Vita is an acronym for Vitality, Innovation, Technology and Ability. In addition, in Italian it means life, reflecting the scientific experiments and the technologies needed for life in space. Additional activities included outreach like Mission-X: Train Like an Astronaut, the European Astro Pi Challenge (where European students run their own code on Raspberry Pi mini computers installed on the ISS).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-VITA-12)

#### VITA mission logo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: VITA mission logo")]

The mission's logo was developed and created jointly by [ESA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESA "ESA"), [Italian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Space_Agency "Italian Space Agency"), and Nespoli. The overall circle represent the planet Earth, with the main objectives linked by a symbol which is a reformulation of the [infinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinity "Infinity") symbol, called "Third paradise" and designed by Michelangelo Pistoletto. Connected inside are a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA "DNA") strand for the scientific experiments, a book for education, outreach and culture, and Earth as a symbol of humanity. The colors represent the Italian flag.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-Vita_logo-13)

#### Mission highlights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mission highlights")]

During the VITA Mission Nespoli completed more than 60 experiments.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-landing-14) He also recorded the first content created in space specifically for use on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-Mabbett-1) During his first month in orbit Nespoli acted as cinematographer for National Geographic Channel's _[One Strange Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Strange\_Rock "One Strange Rock")_, filming the sequences with astronaut [Peggy Whitson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggy_Whitson "Peggy Whitson") which appear in episode 10 of the series.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-15)

Nespoli returned to Earth on 14 December 2017. The [Soyuz MS-05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_MS-05 "Soyuz MS-05") landed at 8:38 UTC,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-landing-14) giving a mission duration of 138 days, 16 hours, 56 minutes and 37 seconds.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-spacefacts53-16)

Major **Paolo Angelo Nespoli** (born 6 April 1957) is an Italian [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineer "Engineer") of the European Space Agency (ESA). In 2007, he first traveled into space aboard the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") as a mission specialist of STS-120. In December 2010 he again traveled into space aboard the [Soyuz TMA-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-20 "Soyuz TMA-20") spacecraft as an [Expedition 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_26 "Expedition 26")/[27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_27 "Expedition 27")[flight engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_engineer "Flight engineer"). Nespoli's third spaceflight was on board [Soyuz MS-05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_MS-05 "Soyuz MS-05"), which launched in July 2017 for [Expedition 52](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_52 "Expedition 52")/[53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_53 "Expedition 53"). He was also the European Space Agency's oldest active astronaut prior to his retirement in 2019.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

Nespoli's hometown is [Verano Brianza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verano_Brianza "Verano Brianza"), in northern Italy. He is married to Russian[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-2) Alexandra Ryabova, and they have one daughter and a son. Nespoli enjoys Scuba diving, piloting aircraft, photography, and building electronic equipment and computer software.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-3) He supports [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") team [Inter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_A._Nespoli#cite_note-4)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paolo_Nespoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Education")]

He received his bachelor's degree in Aerospace engineering in 1988 and his master's degree in 1989 in Aeronautics and Astronautics from [Polytechnic University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polytechnic_Institute_of_New_York_University "Polytechnic Institute of New York University") in New York.

He is a professional engineer, a private pilot, an advanced [scuba diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuba_diver "Scuba diver"), and a [nitrox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrox "Nitrox") diver. Due to his military background, he is also a master parachutist, parachute instructor, jump master, high altitude low opening and [Special Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Forces "Special Forces") operator in the [9th Paratroopers Assault Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Paratroopers_Assault_Regiment "9th Paratroopers Assault Regiment"). He joined the [Italian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Army "Italian Army") in 1977.
